To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most significant association was found with the GCK1 SNP rs730497 (intron 1) in African American T2DM-ESRD patients.
we found linkage and association evidence for GCK1 and other genes in the region.
we identified a linkage peak at 7p in a T2D-ASPs with ESRD and that a variant in GCK1 was associated with T2D and ESRD age at diagnosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes and genetic variants that may contribute to the risk of ESRD in African Americans.
the role of GCK1 in the development of T2D and ESRD in African Americans.
the genetic architecture of T2D-renal disease in African Americans and the genetic determinants of T2D and T2D-related traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study does not provide evidence of a significant role for GCK1, IL-6, IGFB1, and IGFBP-3 in T2D or T2D- ESRD in African Americans.
this study did not identify a major locus for T2D-ERSD in this African American sample.
the region on chromosome 7 harbors a locus that contributes to the development of early-onset type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GCK1 may play a role in T2D and T2D-related complications in African Americans.
GCK1 is a candidate gene in the linkage region on 7p for T2D-renal complications in African Americans.
the GCK1 region may be a susceptibility locus for early-onset TID-ESRD in African Americans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GCK1 locus is associated with early onset ESRD.
linkage and association studies in African Americans are possible, and can be useful for the discovery of genetic factors that influence T2D- related complications.
linkage studies can be used to fine map regions of interest, and then association studies can be used for further refinement of the region.
